cards.headline: Night-owl volume bidder who lives in the cap-free pool and inflates prices as a serial underbidder, but rarely closes the marquee — a nuisance and price-pusher, not a marquee rival to Keith.
cards.bid_rhythm: Hard nocturnal. SF-era peak_hours_et = 23, 22, 13, and the hour_hist bears it out: 43 bids land in the 23:00 ET hour and 32 in the 22:00 hour — by far the heaviest two buckets, dwarfing every daytime hour. There is a secondary ~13:00 ET (1pm) lunch pulse (13 bids). High raw volume — 233 bids for only 60 wins (~3.9 bids per win) spread broadly — but the clicking concentrates into the 10pm–midnight ET window. Expect him most live when other owners are asleep.
cards.snipe_threat: Real and his standout trait. post_win_pounce_share = 0.65 — after ~two-thirds of his wins he is bidding on another lot within 8h — and post_win_avg_followups = 2.47, so each win tends to spawn ~2-3 more bids. Winning a lot does not pull him out of the room; it accelerates him into a chain of further pickups in the same late-night session. Practical read: if Keith wins a lot, Ryan won't retaliate on that lot, but he'll immediately swing at whatever else is still open.
cards.lurk_threat: High-frequency underbidder, low conversion. runner_up_n = 43 in the SF era (51 over L5) — his bridesmaid count nearly matches his 60 wins, so he is constantly the guy who pushes the winner up and then loses. lurk_win_n = 0: sitting as the underbidder essentially never converts to a win for him. late_bid_share is only moderate (under8h 0.348, under6h 0.326, under2h 0.287) — about a third of his action is inside the final 8h, but he is not a true last-second sniper; most overtakes land 24–90h out (Mike Evans pushed to $36k bumping 0010 at 45.3h, Hopkins to $26k at 43.2h). overtake_rate 0.245, late_overtake_n only 7. Net: he inflates prices far more than he steals lots.
cards.spend_signature: Bargain-bin specialist. zone_mix = capfree 0.733 / low 0.117 / mid 0.083 / marquee 0.067 — far more cap-free-skewed than the league (league capfree 0.611, marquee 0.126), i.e. he plays marquee about half as often as the field. Only 4 marquee_wins and a max_win_k of just $38k (Derek Carr, 2022) — well under the league's top SF wins ($94k Henry, $66k Brady). SF positional spend tilts WR $65k / QB $64k / RB $64k, then TE $35k and LB $23k — note the meaningful LB line for an offense-heavy field. He spreads $286k across 60 wins (~$4.8k avg, right at the league median win of $4k), confirming a wide-and-shallow, value-hunting style rather than star-hunting.
cards.vs_0008: Medium threat to Keith — disruptive on the margins, not at the top. (1) PRICE-PUSHER, not a thief: with runner_up_n 43 and lurk_win_n 0, Ryan's main effect on Keith is bidding Keith's targets up and then bowing out; Keith can let Ryan run the early price and still expect to win contested lots, since Ryan rarely converts. (2) He has already poked Keith 7 times in the SF era (overtakes vs victim_fid 0008): Trubisky $5k, Russell Gage $5k, Mike Evans $5k, Spillane $2k, Flacco $2k, Rousseau $2k, Aubrey $2k — every single one cheap/cap-free, never a marquee fight. So the clash zone is the $2–5k scrap pool, not Keith's big swings. (3) TIMING: Keith should place real bids in the 10pm–midnight ET window only if he intends to win, because that's Ryan's active hour and he'll volume-bid filler up; conversely, lots Keith genuinely wants are safer parked when Ryan is offline (early/mid afternoon outside the 1pm pulse). (4) POUNCE GUARD: after Keith wins anything, expect Ryan to immediately work other open lots (pounce 0.65, ~2.5 followups) — so if Keith and Ryan share a watchlist of cheap LBs/QBs, get the must-haves locked early rather than leaving them in the late pool where Ryan is chaining. Bottom line: don't overpay to out-muscle him on marquee (he won't be there), but don't leave cheap targets exposed in his 22:00–23:00 ET prime time.
key_examples: 2022: Won Derek Carr (QB) for $38k — his single largest SF-era win and one of only 4 marquee_wins; got there by overtaking 0002 up the ladder, illustrating he'll commit at QB but tops out ~$38k vs the league's $66k QB ceiling.

2022: Pushed Mike Evans (WR) to $36k as the underbidder against 0010 and LOST, then again chased Evans to $21k in 2024 (vs 0012) and lost — a textbook runner_up_n=43 pattern of inflating a star's price without closing.

SF-era overtakes directly against Keith (0008) are all cap-free scraps: Mitch Trubisky $5k (2022), Russell Gage $5k (2022), Mike Evans $5k (2024), Robert Spillane LB $2k, Joe Flacco $2k, Greg Rousseau DE $2k, Brandon Aubrey PK $2k (all 2024-25) — the Keith collision zone is the $2–5k bin, never the marquee.

Pounce in action: in 2022 he won Bobby Wagner (LB, $9k) and Robert Woods (WR, $13k) and Derek Carr ($38k) within the same active stretch — consistent with post_win_pounce_share 0.65 / 2.47 followups, where one win triggers a chain of further late-night bids.

cards.headline: A cap-free grinder who mostly nibbles, but will lurch awake to snipe a marquee WR/RB right at the 24h lock — and twice has ripped a built-up lot straight out of Keith's hands.
cards.bid_rhythm: Early-morning bidder: SF peak_hours_et are 8, 9, 0 (his hour_hist spikes at hr8=22 and hr9=19, plus an overnight/midnight cluster of 18 at hr0). Activity is spread across the clock rather than one window, but the live danger sits in the morning ET hours and at midnight, not the evening. His bids run LATE in the lock cycle: SF late_bid_share is under8h 0.369, under6h 0.352, under2h 0.336 — over a third of his bids land with under 2h on the clock, so he is a back-half-of-the-window operator who lets a lot ripen and pounces near close.
cards.snipe_threat: Real post-win activity: SF post_win_pounce_share is 0.423 with post_win_avg_followups 1.25 (L5 nearly identical: 0.417 / 1.28). So after roughly 4 of every 10 wins he immediately bids on at least one more lot within 8h, averaging ~1.25 follow-ups. He is not a relentless serial sniper, but a win does NOT take him out of the room — expect one or two opportunistic follow-on bids while Keith is still mid-fight on the next player.
cards.lurk_threat: Genuine lurk/late-overtake threat. SF runner_up_n=18 (L5=23) — he is frequently the underbidder/bridesmaid who pushes the winner up and loses, so he is constantly applying price pressure even when he walks away empty. His SF overtake_rate is 0.133 with late_overtake_n=1 (L5 late_overtake_n=3): he rarely waits til the final 2h to do the overtaking, but he DOES swoop. Documented: 2024 Kamara — Keith (0008) built the lot to 26k, then at the 24h mark 0002 came over the top at 27k (is_overtake=1, victim_fid=0008, seq17) and won at 27k. He sits as the second-highest bidder more than almost anything else he does.
cards.spend_signature: Overwhelmingly a cap-free dabbler: SF zone_mix is capfree 0.865 / low 0.058 / mid 0.038 / marquee 0.038 — 86.5% of his action is the 2-4K bargain bin (vs league capfree 0.611). But he carries a marquee streak: SF marquee_wins=2, max_win_k=32.0 (DeAndre Hopkins 2022), and his all-time book includes Antonio Brown at 79k (2019) and Keenan Allen at 60k (2021), so he can detonate. Position appetite tilts pass-catcher/back: SF pos_spend_k WR 55k, RB 42k, QB 28k — exactly Keith's wheelhouse. 52 SF wins on 180 bids, total 172k.
cards.vs_0008: He directly collides with Keith on the positions Keith spends on (WR 55k / RB 42k SF) and has TWICE won a lot that 0008 was actively building. 2022 Hopkins: Keith opened at 1k, 0002 overtook him at 5k (vic=0008) and then late-laddered 27→28→32k to win at 32k. 2024 Kamara: Keith pushed it to 26k, 0002 sniped at 27k over the top of 0008 at the 24h lock and won. Across his book he forced/pushed 0008 on 17 separate bids (Edelman 30k 2014, Kamara 27k, Hopkins). And in 2021 he won Keenan Allen at 60k with 0008 as the runner_up — Keith was the bridesmaid that time. Handling: do NOT let Whitman set the closing price on a WR/RB Keith truly wants — his danger is concentrated in the morning ET hours (8-9) and the final-2h window (33.6% of bids under 2h), so Keith should place his decisive ladder bid AFTER Whitman's typical morning/late surge or be prepared to jump him at the lock rather than nominate-and-coast. Because 86.5% of his bids are cap-free junk, treat his early 2-4k pokes as noise; the tell that he is serious is a mid-window jump on a marquee WR/RB — that's when to either commit hard early or let him have it, never leave a half-built marquee lot exposed at the 24h mark.
key_examples: 2022 DeAndre Hopkins (WR): Keith (0008) opened at 1k; 0002 overtook 0008 at 5k (seq3, vic=0008), then late-laddered 27→28→32k inside the final 24h to WIN at 32k — his SF max_win and a marquee_win, taken off a Keith-opened lot.

2024 Alvin Kamara (RB): Keith built the price to 26k (seq16); at the 24h lock 0002 came over the top at 27k (seq17, is_overtake=1, victim_fid=0008) and won at 27k — a textbook late-overtake snipe on a Keith-built RB.

2021 Keenan Allen (WR): 0002 WON at 60k with runner_up_fid=0008 — Keith was the underbidder who pushed Whitman to his second-highest career price; proof Whitman will chase a marquee WR all the way up against Keith.
2019 Antonio Brown (WR): all-time max win at 79k — evidence that despite an 86.5% cap-free SF profile, Whitman is capable of a true marquee detonation when motivated.

cards.headline: A relentless cap-free grinder who lurks late, overtakes often, and has personally jacked up Keith's price on a marquee RB.
cards.bid_rhythm: Daytime-active and spread across the clock. SF peak ET hours are 12, 14, 16 (a midday-into-afternoon window), with secondary spikes at hours 9, 17, and 20. The L5 hour_hist also lights up hour 0 (20 bids) and hour 20 (19), so he is reachable from noon to late night, not a single tight window. Critically he bids LATE: 52.2% of SF bids land under 8h to close, 50.0% under 6h, and 47.1% under 2h — nearly half his action is in the final two hours before the 24h lock.
cards.snipe_threat: Real and consistent. post_win_pounce_share is 0.522 in SF (0.518 over L5) with post_win_avg_followups of 1.15 — after winning a lot he bids on another within 8h more than half the time. He does not bank a win and go quiet; expect him to immediately roll momentum into a second target, so his wins should be treated as a signal to recheck your own watchlist, not relief.
cards.lurk_threat: High. He is the prototype underbidder/bridesmaid: runner_up_n is 17 in SF (25 over L5) — he loses a lot of bid wars, but only after pushing the winner's price up. overtake_rate 0.183 with late_overtake_n 8 (11 over L5) means he actively re-bids in the closing hours: of 38 SF overtakes, multiple land inside the final ~36h (e.g. 2025 Etienne at $16 t_close 24.02h over 0004; 2024 Henry at $34 t_close 24.04h over 0002; 2024 Singletary at $21 t_close 24.03h over 0001). lurk_win_n is 0, so he rarely steals the lot outright — his weapon is the late tax he applies on the way to losing.
cards.spend_signature: Volume-over-stars value hunter. SF zone_mix is 80.6% cap-free (2-4K), 7.5% low, just 1.5% mid, and 10.4% marquee — far more cap-free-skewed than the league (61.1% cap-free / 12.6% marquee). 67 SF wins on 208 bids for $311K total. Position spend (SF) leans RB $94K, QB $70K, WR $67K, TE $33K, with a real IDP appetite (LB $15K, S $9K). marquee_wins 7, max_win_k $37K (Kirk Cousins QB, 2022). Other marquee wins: Derrick Henry RB $34K (2024), Chris Godwin WR $27K (2023), David Njoku TE $27K (2025), Devin Singletary RB $21K (2024), D.J. Moore WR $21K (2025), Sam Darnold QB $18K (2025). He will splurge a few times a summer but lives in the cap-free bargain bin.
cards.vs_0008: Gerardi is a direct, repeat antagonist on Keith's lots. In the SF era he has overtaken 0008 four times: Kamara $5K (2024), Travis Kelce $12K (2025), Deebo Samuel $7K t_close 24.02h (2025), and most importantly Chuba Hubbard $34K (2025). The Hubbard war is the tell — Keith opened the bidding ($15→$20), Gerardi climbed in at $23→$24→$26→$28 then overtook Keith directly at $34 (seq11), forcing Keith to grind up to $36→$37 to finally win at $37 (a $17 premium over Keith's $20 opener that Gerardi personally manufactured). Tactic vs 0008: (1) Because he is a cap-free grinder, do NOT engage him in the 2-4K bin — he will outlast you on volume and it is wasted ammo; concede the scraps. (2) On YOUR marquee RB/WR/TE targets, expect him to appear late (sub-2h) and as an overtaker, so do not show your ceiling early — his 47.1% sub-2h share means a comfortable lead at hour 12 is not safe at hour 23. Place your true max in the final window so he cannot ratchet you up incrementally like he did on Hubbard. (3) Treat any Gerardi win as a snipe warning (52.2% pounce) and re-cover your other open lots immediately. (4) His IDP/TE spend (Njoku $27K, LB $15K) overlaps Keith's needs — pre-empt those at a price above his marquee comfort to avoid a bidding ladder.
key_examples: 2025 Chuba Hubbard RB: Gerardi (0003) climbed $23→$28 then overtook Keith (0008) at $34 with 35h left (seq11); Keith was forced up to $37 to win — Gerardi added roughly $17 to Keith's bill on a lot he did not even win.
2022 Kirk Cousins QB $37K — his max win and a marquee QB grab, overtaking 0010 from $17; shows he will go to the top of the QB market when motivated.
2024 Derrick Henry RB $34K, won at hour 19 with t_close 24.04h after overtaking 0002 — a late-window marquee overtake that became a win.
2025 Deebo Samuel WR: Gerardi overtook Keith (0008) at $7K with just 24.02h to close — a textbook late re-bid directly on a Keith lot.

cards.headline: A heavy-spending RB/QB whale who dawn-patrols the board, pounces on 67% of his wins, and has already pushed Keith to a $94K record and out-dueled him for Kelce.
cards.bid_rhythm: Hard morning bidder: SF-era peak_hours_et are 6, 7, 12 ET, with the hour_hist stacking 42 bids at 6am and 38 at 7am ET (vs only a few in the 17:00-21:00 evening window). He fires when most owners are asleep, then a midday top-up at noon (30 bids in the 12:00 bucket). Not primarily a last-second sniper — late_bid_share is moderate (under8h 0.244, under6h 0.228, under2h 0.191), so ~1 in 5 of his bids land in the final 2 hours but the bulk are placed early and often (300 SF-era bids for only 61 wins).
cards.snipe_threat: Elite pouncer — this is his most dangerous trait. SF-era post_win_pounce_share is 0.672 (he bids on another lot within 8h of two-thirds of his wins) with post_win_avg_followups 2.64. Verified in the DB: the minute after winning McCaffrey at 07:47:30 (2025) he was bidding Aiyuk at 07:48:44 and Njoku ($16K) at 07:49:26, then chased Etienne, Kelce, and Rodgers across the same day. Winning one lot does NOT take him off the board; it accelerates him.
cards.lurk_threat: Real bridesmaid/late-overtake threat. runner_up_n is 24 (SF) — he is frequently the underbidder who drives the price up and loses. late_overtake_n is 7 with overtake_rate 0.27, and he will jump late to steal: on his own McCaffrey 2025 win he sat at $45K then leaped to $56K at 20:44 ET to lock it. His losses cluster on premium RB/QB: he pushed Ekeler to $57K (lost to 0009, 2022), Prescott to $50K (lost to 0002, 2024), and Tyreek Hill to $61K (lost to 0007, 2024) — meaning his presence inflates every marquee skill-position lot whether or not he wins it.
cards.spend_signature: Top-of-market money concentrated on RB and QB. SF-era total_k 430 across 61 wins; pos_spend_k is RB 125 / QB 106 / WR 71 / TE 47 — RB+QB = 54% of spend. zone_mix is capfree 0.672 / low 0.131 / mid 0.082 / marquee 0.115, and he has 7 marquee_wins (18K+) in the SF era: McCaffrey $56K, Prescott $45K, Mayfield $31K, Davante Adams $30K, Keenan Allen $28K, Goedert $22K, Kelce $21K. max_win_k is 56.0 (McCaffrey 2025). He is comfortable spending into the p90+ of every position (league RB p90 is 27K, QB p90 38K — he routinely clears both).
cards.vs_0008: Direct, proven antagonist to Keith. In 2023 0004 was the runner-up who forced Keith (0008) to the league-record $94K for Derrick Henry — his own top bid hit $65K and his $54K/$52K bids list 0008 as the party he was forcing. That cost Keith ~$40K of cap he wouldn't have spent unopposed. In 2025 0004 BEAT Keith head-to-head for Travis Kelce ($21K, with Keith as the forced underbidder at the $9-10K rungs). Tactics for Keith: (1) Expect him on every premium RB/QB Keith nominates — bake a 0004 premium into the budget or nominate Keith's RB/QB targets at off-hours he's less active. (2) Beat his dawn patrol — get a firm lead in before the 6-7am ET window or be ready to defend at noon; do not assume a quiet overnight lot is safe. (3) Respect the late jump — he overtook from $45K to $56K on his own McCaffrey win, so a comfortable evening lead on a marquee player is not safe from him near close. (4) Use him as a price-setter against others: he will inflate a lot then lose (runner_up_n 24), so if Keith doesn't want the player, let 0004 bid the field up and bleed a rival's cap.
key_examples: Derrick Henry 2023 RB: 0004 was the underbidder who pushed Keith (0008) to the league-record $94K, topping out at his own $65K bid and forcing 0008 at the $54K/$52K rungs — directly cost Keith cap.

Christian McCaffrey 2025 RB ($56K, his max win): sat at $45K then late-overtook to $56K at 20:44 ET, and one minute after the 07:47 lock was already bidding Aiyuk (07:48) and Njoku $16K (07:49) — pounce in action.
Travis Kelce 2025 TE ($21K win): out-dueled Keith (0008) head-to-head, with Keith left as the forced underbidder at the $9-10K rungs.

Marquee losses where he inflated the price and bowed out: Ekeler $57K (to 0009, 2022), Prescott $50K (to 0002, 2024), Tyreek Hill $61K (to 0007, 2024) — runner_up_n 24 confirms he is a serial price-driver.

cards.headline: A morning-shift RB/QB bully who has out-muscled Keith 11-2 in head-to-head lots and pounces on a second target after almost every win.
cards.bid_rhythm: Daytime/early aggressor, NOT a midnight sniper. SF-era peak ET hours are 5, 12, 8 (hour_hist: 27 bids at 5am, 24 at noon, 18 at 8am ET; next cluster is 0:00 with 12). The headline late_bid_share (under8h 0.306 / under6h 0.290 / under2h 0.258) is misleading — strip the auto-close rows and only 2 of his 174 SF bids were genuinely placed with <8h left (Conner $38k at 0.03h, Hines $8k at 4.5h). His real M.O. is to seize the lead DAYS early: of 53 SF overtakes, nearly all land at t_to_close of 24-100h, not the final hours. Focused morning/lunch windows, not a wide spread.
cards.snipe_threat: Heavy pouncer — his most dangerous trait for board flow. post_win_pounce_share 0.705 (SF) / 0.711 (L5): after ~7 of every 10 wins he's bidding on another lot within 8h, averaging 1.39 follow-ups (SF) / 1.89 (L5). He doesn't bank a win and rest — landing a player triggers him to immediately go shopping again. Expect him to win a target and then appear on the very next RB/QB you nominate.
cards.lurk_threat: Active overtaker, not a passive lurker (lurk_win_n=0 — he never sits quiet as the underbidder to steal at the buzzer). overtake_rate 0.305 across 53 SF overtakes, but late_overtake_n is only 3 — his overtakes are early, not last-second. He is a frequent bridesmaid though: runner_up_n=8 (SF) / 14 (L5), and a broader cut shows him pushing the eventual winner up on 16 SF lots (Fournette to $39k after he hit $35k; Conner to $38k matching his own $38k; Godwin to $27k). He inflates prices even when he loses.
cards.spend_signature: RB-first, QB-second. SF pos_spend: RB $122k, QB $75k, WR $49k, then IDP (LB $21k, S $20k, DE $13k); $319k total over 61 wins. Mostly value-shopping — zone_mix is 78.7% cap-free (2-4K), only ~8% each mid and marquee — but he WILL spike: marquee_wins=5, max_win $41k (Mixon 2023). Big wins: Mixon RB $41k, Tagovailoa QB $29k, Matt Ryan QB $28k, Mostert RB $20k, Ridley WR $18k. League SF context: median win is just $4k, so his spikes move the market (RB p95 $39k, QB p95 $50k).
cards.vs_0008: Direct, repeated collision in Keith's core lanes. In 21 SF-era lots where both bid, Hammer won 11 and Keith won only 2 — and he overtook Keith (victim_fid=0008) six times: Mixon RB ($23k push), Godwin WR ($13k), Marquise Brown WR twice ($13k/$19k), Noah Fant TE ($3k), Diggs WR ($5k). His RB/QB-heavy spend overlaps Keith's positions almost exactly, so he's the owner most likely on the other side of your nominations. Handling: (1) He moves EARLY — don't out-wait him; by the time the clock's low he's usually already leading, so commit your real number up front. (2) Use his pounce reflex: nominate a tempting cap-free RB right after he just won one — he'll likely engage and burn cap/attention while your real target sits quiet. (3) On marquee RB/QB he tops out near $41k and rarely sustains marquee; go past ~$42k and you can break him, but expect him to push you the whole way (he matched Keith dollar-for-dollar on Mixon $41k and Mostert $20k before the tiebreak). (4) Don't get baited into bidding wars on mid-tier RBs — that's exactly where his 11-2 edge lives.
key_examples: 2023 Joe Mixon (RB) — Hammer's max win at $41k; he overtook Keith (0008) en route at $23k, then matched Keith dollar-for-dollar at $41k and won the tiebreak. Textbook 'wins the exact RB Keith wants.'
2023 Marquise Brown (WR) — Hammer overtook Keith TWICE (to $13k then $19k) and pushed the lot to $27k before losing to 0011 at $37k; a pure price-inflator who cost both Keith and the winner real cap.

2024 Noah Fant (TE) & 2025 Stefon Diggs (WR) — both lots he overtook Keith (0008) directly; on Fant he forced Keith up to the $4k winning bid, on Diggs he pushed Keith to a $14k commitment. He engages Keith specifically even on small lots.
2022 & 2024 Mostert / 2025 Geno Smith — three SF lots Hammer won outright over Keith (RB $11k, RB $20k, QB $15k), illustrating his 11-2 head-to-head dominance in the RB/QB lanes Keith plays.

cards.headline: A relentless cap-free grinder who lives at the bottom of the board and quietly muscles Keith on cheap-to-mid RBs.

But note the followups are almost all cap-free/cheap dart-throws ($2-4k), not marquee swoops — he keeps the conveyor belt moving rather than escalating into a big lot.

SF-era runner_up_n=21 (28 over L5) — he is frequently the bridesmaid who pushes the winner up and loses. overtake_rate is only 0.19 with late_overtake_n=5, and lurk_win_n=0, so he forces prices but rarely steals lots late. Concrete pushes: David Montgomery 2025 (bid to $17k, lost to 0001 at $20k), Stefon Diggs 2025 (to $12k, lost to 0001 at $20k), Allen Robinson 2022 (to $12k, lost to 0009 at $21k), Myles Garrett 2023 (to $7k, lost to 0007 at $13k). cards.spend_signature: Deep-value specialist. SF-era zone_mix is 87.2% cap-free (2-4k), 8.5% low, 2.1% mid, 2.1% marquee — by far a bottom-of-the-board operator (vs league cap-free share 61.1%). 47 wins on only 132k total = ~2.8k/win, right around the league median win of 4k. Top positions by spend: RB 63k, LB 19k, WR 17k, QB 11k. marquee_wins=1, max_win_k=22 (Kareem Hunt 2022 — his lone real splurge). His one big historical splash was Robert Woods at $41k in 2021 (pre-SF). He almost never plays in the 18k+ marquee tier where Keith's stars live.
cards.vs_0008: The overlap is RBs at the low-to-mid tier, and it is real. Direct SF-era collisions: he beat Keith for Cooper Kupp 2025 ($9k vs Keith's $7k), beat Keith for Najee Harris 2025 ($13k vs $8k), and tied Keith on Austin Ekeler 2025 (both at $8k, Keith won) and Keaton Mitchell ($2k each, 0006 won). With RB his #1 spend (63k SF) and ~41% of bids in the final 2 hours, he is exactly the guy who nudges Keith's value-RB targets up a tick or two in the closing window — death by a thousand cuts, not a knockout. Handling: do NOT bid early against him on a cheap RB (you just teach him the price and invite a late push); set a firm walk-away and be willing to let him have the $2-4k dart-throws — his pounce conveyor wants volume, not your $13k. On a genuine mid-RB you want (the Najee/Kupp tier), bid to your max in one clean overnight-ET move to close before his under-2h window opens, since he overtakes late only 19% of the time and has zero lurk-wins. He is NOT a marquee threat — your 18k+ stars are safe from him.
key_examples: Najee Harris (RB, 2025): 0006 won at $13k, directly outbidding Keith/0008's $8k — RB-vs-Keith collision he won.
Cooper Kupp (WR, 2025): 0006 won at $9k over Keith's $7k; one of the rare WRs where he closed.

takeaways: The PF bar to be a top-2 all-play team since Superflex (2022) is ~3,160-3,280 PF. The eight top-2 finishers ranged 3,084-3,338, with seven of eight at 3,160+. Median top-2 PF is ~3,224.

Across all four seasons the #1 all-play team landed at .717 win pct three times (134-53 in 2023/2024/2025) and .706 once (2022). The #2 team ranged .636-.706. So to be a genuine top-2 team you need roughly a .68+ all-play win pct, i.e. ~128+ all-play wins out of 187.

PF and all-play win pct are tightly coupled but not identical: in 2022 Good in Da Hood led the entire league in PF (3338.7) yet finished #2 all-play behind C-Town (3084.3), and in 2025 C-Town had the league-high PF (3218.6) but the 2nd-best win pct. Scoring volume is the dominant driver of contention, but week-to-week consistency separates #1 from #2.

For franchise 0008 (Real Deal Creel / Keith), the contention gap is concrete: best finish since Superflex was 2023 at 105-82 (.561, PF 3046.5) and 2024 at 96-91 (.513, PF 3027.6). To reach the top-2 bar the roster needs roughly +130 to +250 PF per season (from ~3,030 to ~3,160-3,280) and ~+25 to +35 all-play wins. 2025 was a down year at 77-110 (.412, PF 2912) — the largest gap to close.

The contender PF threshold has been stable, not inflating: top-2 PF sat 3,084-3,338 in 2022 and 3,197-3,218 in 2025. There is no scoring arms race to chase — hitting ~3,200 PF reliably has been good enough for top-2 every year.
